production.note: US model years. The R35 GT-R is split into records by year range because its US power rating changed too much for one figure (480 hp in 2009, 565 hp from 2017). First: Nissan's release 'All-New 2009 Nissan GT-R Comes to North America'. Last: the 2011 press kit (nissan-us-2011-gt-r-press-kit); for 2012 Nissan says the engine "now produces 530 horsepower (versus the previous 485 horsepower)" (nissan-us-2012-gt-r-press-kit), which starts the 2012–2016 record.

body.note: Inferred from Nissan's description of the two-door, four-passenger GT-R; the kit does not use the word coupe. The databases list the styles as 'GT-R Coupe 2D' and 'GT-R Premium Coupe 2D' (kbb-gt-r-2010-specs).

displacementL.note: Nissan's US kit gives litres only ('3.8-liter'). Nissan's US heritage page gives '3796 cc' for the VR38DETT (nissan-us-heritage-2008-gt-r), which also rounds to 3.8.

fuel.note: Inferred from the kit's description of the twin-turbo petrol V6.

drivetrain.note: 'Electronically-controlled ATTESA E-TS all-wheel-drive system specifically developed for GT-R'

transmission.note: 'paddle-shifted sequential six-speed dual clutch transmission; manual and automatic modes'. The only transmission.

powerHp.note: 2010 model year, GT-R and GT-R Premium. Quote: "For 2010, the horsepower rating of the GT-R's 3.8-liter twin turbo V6 engine has been increased to 485 hp (from 480 hp)". 485 hp applied to 2010 and 2011, two of this record's three model years: 2011 "485 horsepower at 6,400 rpm and 434 lb-ft of torque at 3,200" (nissan-us-2011-gt-r-press-kit). The 2009 car was rated 480 hp: "480 horsepower @ 6,400 rpm" (nissan-us-2009-gt-r-release).

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL: spec databases only. 2010 base GT-R (2dr Coupe, the standard car), 6-speed dual-clutch. Three databases agree. Edmunds: "Curb weight | 3,814 lbs." (2dr Coupe AWD). Cars.com: "Base Curb Weight: 3,814 lbs" (cars-com-gt-r-2010-specs). KBB: "3,814 pounds" for the GT-R Coupe 2D and "3,829 pounds" for the GT-R Premium Coupe 2D (kbb-gt-r-2010-specs). Nissan's 2009 to 2011 US press kits give no curb weight; Nissan's 2012 kit gives 3,829 lb for the Premium, the same as KBB's 2010 Premium figure.

sources.title: All-New 2009 Nissan GT-R Comes to North America

discrepancies.reason: Model year. Nissan rated the 2009 car at 480 hp and the 2010 and 2011 cars at 485 hp.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 485 hp: it applied to two of the three model years this record covers, and the reference model year is 2010.

provisionalNote: Weight is provisional: 3,814 lb for the 2010 base GT-R rests on Edmunds, Cars.com and KBB (databases, all three agree). Nissan's 2009 to 2011 US press kits give no curb weight. A Nissan US specification table for 2010 or 2011, or a Car and Driver, Road & Track or MotorTrend spec panel for a 2010 or 2011 GT-R, would replace it. All other fields come from Nissan.
